content: Since the input to a language model is a large corpus or set of sentences, one can generalize language modeling approaches to graphs by noting that the analog of a sentence in graphs is a “random walk”. More specifically, note that a truncated random walk of length T starting from a node “v” is analogous to a sentence and effectively captures the context of “v" in the network. More precisely, the same machinery used to learn representations of words in language models can now be adapted to learn deep contextualized representations of knowledge graphs.
